11.processing_rules:
The host always uses a Block Number to track the data block it
sends in an Electronic Mail response and a CA Public Key File
Load response. If response processing is interrupted, the host
knows the Block Number for the last complete data block sent in
the response.
A device is not required to track the Block Number it receives in
an Electronic Mail response. If it is required to do so, and
processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device
can reinstate transmission of the interrupted data block using that
Block Number in the next Electronic Mail request it sends to the
host.
A device always uses a Block Number to track the data block it
sends in a Proprietary Data Load request. If request processing is
interrupted, the host knows the Block Number for the last
complete data block sent in the request.
A device is required to track the Block Number it receives in a CA
Public Key File Load response. If CA Public Key File Load
processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device
reinstates transmission of the interrupted data block using that
Block Number in the next request it sends to the host.

12.processing_rules:
The format varies, depending on the application.
If the Account Number is obtained from a Track 2 card reader,
instead of being manually keyed, the Account Number and Card
Discretionary Block Data should consist of all data read from the
card between, but not including, the Start Sentinel and End
Sentinel. Account Number is considered the data before the =
character, and Card Discretionary Block Data is considered the
data after the = character. The = character is used instead of a
Field Separator.
If the Account Number is obtained from a Track 1 card reader
(credit cards only), instead of being manually keyed, the Account
Number and Card Discretionary Block Data should consist of all
unaltered data read from the card between, but not including, the
Start Sentinel and End Sentinel. Account Number is considered
the data before the first ^ character, and Card Discretionary Block
Data is considered the data after the first ^ character. The ^
character is used instead of a Field Separator.
Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data combined do
not exceed 76 characters for Track 1 or 37 characters for Track 2.
Note: Track data placed in the combined data elements of
Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data cannot
exceed the total length of those data elements
For either TransArmor processing method, the expiration date
must be included here. The expiration date is stored for follow-on
transactions associated with a Token.
Real Time Account Updater:
When a merchant receives Account Updater Expiration Date (New
Expiration Date) in the original transaction response in the Real
Time Account Updater Response Segment – Segment 155, the
merchant can send either the new expiration date or the original
expiration date in the ‘Follow-on’ transactions in this Card
Discretionary Block Data field.
A merchant should send the Expiration Date corresponding to the
original PAN or the new PAN / the original or the new TransArmor
Token that is being sent in the cardholder Account Number field –
Data Element 2 in the Standard Message Data Segment 100.
Software Version: ATL105

can follow the last data element in the message:
• Additional Information Data Segment (Data Segment No. 112)

data segment always follow this data element;
• Element No. 63, Number of Segments

and data segment always follow this data element;
• Element No. 63, Number of Segments
• Data Segment No. 108, Loyalty Card Data Segment
For Electronic Mail Request messages, the following data element
and data segment always follow this data element;
